fields.h1: Build a Training Request Form That Routes Approvals by Cost
fields.hero_description: Get a training request form that totals each course's costs and sends the request to the right approver by amount.
fields.features_heading: What the Paper Version Leaves to HR
fields.features_subheading: Paper forms collect a course and its cost, then wait for signatures. These six pieces carry each request through to an answer.
fields.feature_1:
Costs that total themselves

Each cost gets its own line, with tuition and travel kept apart, and the form adds them as the employee types. An approver reads the full figure first, with the breakdown below.
fields.feature_2:
A reason written in job terms

The form asks which skill the training teaches and which task it changes. A request that reads "pivot tables for the monthly close" is easier to approve than "spreadsheet class".
fields.feature_3:
Approvers chosen by amount

Set a dollar line, and any request above it goes to a second person after the manager approves. Each of them then gets an alert that carries the costs and the reason.
fields.feature_4:
One queue for the training team

Requests land in a single list marked approved, waitlisted, or declined. When a status changes, the requester gets an email with the new status and the reason behind it.
fields.feature_5:
A budget balance per department

A dashboard subtracts each approved request from the department's yearly training budget. Before saying yes, a manager sees what the request would leave for the year.
fields.feature_6:
Training history in a database you own

Each request and its decision save to a database you own, with finished courses, under the employee's name. At review time, a manager sees what a person asked for and completed.

fields.tab_content_1:
Teagan's $1,180 course arrives with its costs itemized

Teagan Renfro runs a CNC lathe at Cobalt Ridge Fabrication and wants a 3-day CNC programming course. Her request lists $950 in tuition and $230 in travel, with the $1,180 total at the top. The start date field accepts nothing less than 14 days out.
fields.tab_content_2:
Over $1,000, the director approves after the manager

Brightwater Ledger asks for two approvals on any training request over $1,000. Data engineer Yevgenia Fairhurst requested a $1,450 conference pass, and her manager approved it this morning. The app then emailed engineering director Corisande Vail, with the cost and Yevgenia's reason in the message.
fields.tab_content_3:
Waitlisted until July, a request for 14 gets a reason

The training coordinator at Harlow Basin Water District has 9 requests this month in one queue: 5 approved, 3 waitlisted, and 1 declined. Field supervisor Thandeka Lowry asked to train 14 technicians on new work order software. The request waits for the July budget, and her email says so.
fields.tab_content_4:
On a $12,000 budget, a $600 course leaves $3,050

Juniper Wharf Outfitters gives store operations a $12,000 training budget for the year, and $8,350 of it is already approved. Store lead Prosper Strachan has asked for a $600 visual merchandising course. The dashboard shows $3,650 left today and $3,050 if his request goes through, before the regional manager decides.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Training Request Form
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to build a training request form that collects the costs, gets the right approvals, and tracks each decision.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put each cost on its own line
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for the reason in job terms
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down who says yes at each amount before you build anything. One college's HR form says every class and workshop must be pre-approved by the approving supervisor before the form goes to HR.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the program name and the provider, then the dates and where it runs. Add a link field for the provider's page, and the approver can read the agenda without asking for it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give tuition and travel separate fields, add lodging when a trip needs it, and let the form total them. Ask who pays the provider before anyone registers.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for the skill the employee expects to gain and where they will use it at work. One college's form also asks whether the course is a component of the employee's professional development plan.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the fewest days allowed between a request and the course start, and make the date field enforce it. Ask for more lead time on any course that needs flights or a hotel.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Write the waitlist and decline reasons
fields.howto_step_6_des: Draft the short reasons approvers will pick from, such as budget timing or a class already offered in house. The requester gets the reason with the decision instead of a bare no.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Run one past request through it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter a request your team approved last quarter and follow it to the final decision. Fix any step where the approver had to ask a question the form should have answered.

faq_plan.q: What is a training request form?
faq_plan.a: A training request form is the document an employee fills in to ask an employer to approve a class or conference and its cost. It records what the training is, when it runs, what it costs, and why the employee needs it. Training request forms also leave a record of who approved each one and when.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a training request form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: the fields, who approves each request, and what happens after a decision. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the approval logic from that prompt. To change a field or an approver later, ask for the change in a sentence.

faq_plan.q: What should a training request form template ask the employee?
faq_plan.a: A training request form template should ask for the employee's name, role, and department, then the course, provider, dates, each cost, and a reason tied to the job. One L&D intake guide also lists "Target audience and estimated learner count" as a baseline field. The same fields work on a training request form PDF or online.

faq_plan.q: How do you close out a training request form once the course ends?
faq_plan.a: Ask the employee for proof of completion, then mark the request complete. One college's form lists "After event submit proof of completion" as the last step for a workshop or seminar. Send a training feedback form within a few days of the course, while the details are fresh, and file the answers under the original request.

faq_plan.q: Who should sign off on a training request form?
faq_plan.a: The employee's direct supervisor should sign first, because they know whether the course fits the job and the schedule. Above a dollar amount you choose, add a second approver, such as a director or HR, and use the same line for every department. In an app built with Emergent, an approver who has not answered gets a reminder.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead should employees submit a training request form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for at least two weeks before the course starts, unless your own policy sets a longer window. One university policy says employees "should submit out-service training requests at least two weeks in advance" of the training. For a conference with flights and a hotel, ask for a month. Travel then gets booked after approval, not before it.

faq_plan.q: Should a training request form ask for the days away from work?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for the dates and hours the employee will be away, and the supervisor can plan coverage before approving. One university policy says the justification includes the costs and "leave requested, if any" as well. If training days count as leave under the employer's policy, have the employee file a time off request form for the same dates.

faq_plan.q: What should an employee write as the reason on a training request form?
faq_plan.a: Write how the course helps the employer as well as the employee, in a few sentences tied to current work. One university policy wants "ways in which the requested training will benefit the University and the employee" in the justification. A line such as "cuts setup time on the new lathe" gives the approver something to weigh against the cost, and "career growth" alone does not.

faq_plan.q: Can one training request form cover a whole team?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put a request type at the top, individual or group, and show the group questions only when someone picks group, such as the number of learners and their roles. A manager then files one request for the whole team instead of one per person. One L&D intake guide gives the same advice: "Layer in conditional questions that appear based on the request type selected."

faq_plan.q: How should employees record training hours after a training request form is approved?
faq_plan.a: Log them on the time sheet form for the week of the course, under a training code, not regular work. The code ties those hours back to the approved request. Ask your payroll or HR team how training time counts toward paid hours before the course starts. Emergent builds both forms from a prompt, and their data lives in a database you own.

plan.angle: The top 10 is mostly paper: Word files and PDFs from city, county and college HR offices (Dallas, Faribault County, South Texas College), a SHRM form, template sites and an L&D intake article from Cognota. They collect the course, the provider, the dates, the cost and a reason, then wait for signatures. None adds up the costs, sends a request to the right approver by amount, tells a requester why a request is waitlisted or shows what is left in the training budget. This page builds the form with those four jobs: cost lines that total themselves, a second approver above a dollar threshold, one status queue for the training team, and a budget balance per department.
